New treatment for Cerebral Palsy

By: Tarryn Crossman | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
we bring you a groundbreaking treatment for Cerebral Palsey

Summary:
ABR has been available in Europe and Asia for a few years now, but not in South Africa. We speak to two parents who believe ABR has saved their children, Emma and Nathan. Emma's mom is a doctor and would like to bring ABR to South Africa with the help of ABR specialists in Denmark.
Slobodan, the physiotherapist and ABR trainer from Denmark will be coming to South Africa in April to re-evaluate Nathan. We will film this session and speak to him about the details of ABR and how it can be available in South Africa
Dr Peter Rosenburg has written many academic papers on ABR and in 2002 he took the 5 stages of CP and did a study based on specimens to see how effective ABR alone is as a treatment. As apposed to studies on conventional physiotherapy, which showed a slow but gradual decline in the patients, his studies showed that with ABR treatment patient who were in Stage 5 become more mobile and become stage 4 patients. We will be interviewing him over skype.

Further information:
Erika’s daughter Emma was born with Cerebral Palsy, they were living in Sweden when she was diagnosed. After just under 2 years of following the normal therapy regime of OT, Physio and speech therapy Erika saw no improvement in Emma. As a medical doctor, she started doing research and found an alternative treatment having brilliant result on Stage 4 CB patients like her daughter.
The ABR was invented by a mechanical engineer in Russia and works on the basic principle that; to improve a CP patient you have to increase their core strength and create a comfortable rest position for the patient before they can start developing their other finer motor neuron functions. It works with basic equipment and 2 hours of therapy every day, which the parent or caregiver is trained to do. It is non evasive and not exhausting for the patient. But the treatment takes consistency and time to start working.

After the first year Erika noticed remarkable changes in Emma. She could hold her head up for seconds at a time and was beginning to to focus her eyes. She could see her child starting to react emotionally to situations. Emma has been using ABR for 3 years now and from not being able to move her hands, Erika is hopeful that a joystick controlled wheelchair will be possible for her child this year. With her core in place Emma has returned to conventional therapies like OT , speech therapy and Physio as compared to when they first tried these treatment 3 years ago, they are now showing positive results.

Nathan was 17 months old when he becomes another child to fall victim to a freak drowning in South Africa. His parents James and Emmy will forever blame themselves for the rest of their lives for what happened to Nathan that day. As a result of the near drowning, Nathan was left with severe Cerebral Palsy. After months of conventional treatment Nathan's condition was worse than ever. He was unable to eat anything and was put on a permanent feeding tube. His doctors were not convinced that he would make it. As a last resort his parents searched the internet for alternative treatment and found ABR. They brought the ABR trainer over from Denmark and started treating Nathan for 3 hours a day 5 days a week. The transformation was amazing. You can see his full physical change of the video’s the family have filmed. Nathan can hold himself up for periods of time, he is eating and laughing.

Nathan was on various other treatments at the same time though, so medically his improvement can not solely be placed on ABR, but it is his parents’ belief that ABR saved their son.

Press Release:


Innovative Treatment for Cerebral Palsy
Advanced Bio-Mechanical Rehabilitation (ABR) is a revolutionary, non-invasive treatment for children with Cerebral Palsy. It focuses not on the brain, but on core body strength, which is vital in saving the lives of young children with this condition. But in the past this remarkable form of therapy has been available only in Europe and Asia. Carte Blanche meets the desperate parents who are fighting to bring this treatment to hundreds of South African children.


Script:


Time code CHARACTER / VISUAL
1 00:00 Opening with Emma and V/O. Clair Mawisa on camera continues V/O: EMMA Dewes was diagnosed with Cerebral palsy at birth while Nathan Ogrady was diagnosed after a near death drowning. This is how their parents discovered revolutionary new physical therapy that changed both their lives.
2 00:14 Emma at School Teacher: you are going to draw your family? What is mommy doing? Is mommy a doctor? Hey Mommy is a doctor?
3 00:24 Emma’s mother Erika Dewes talks about Emma’s condition. She was born prematurely a baby is suppose to develop in a specific way in the first year and these are called milestone so things like head control, sitting, crawling things that are suppose to happen in the first year and with her it just never happened. Then when we saw the specialist in June she said “she can signs and symptoms of cerebral palsy” which was obviously a devastating thing
4 00:49 Witbank
Claire Mawisa interviews Nathan’s parents about his condition and his story – Emma Truter and James O’grady James: He disappeared under peoples eyes at about five half fast five I pick him out of the water round about ten past 12past five and started CPR immediately, the next door neighbour was a paramedic they rushed him off to the hospital and about an hour later his heart started and his pulse going and got him a bit stable.

Emma: The doctor said to us uhm “ Nathans got sever hyprokstar it’s a brain injury due to lack of oxygen to the brain

Claire: How old was Nathan at the time?
James: He was 17 months and he just started walking and talking and running around.
Claire: what were the initial treatments that you tried?
Emma: physic, OT and Speech.
James: He was on spinneret for epilepsy; he was on Baculiform for spasms and for Cinnamet for parkinsons because he was not sure if he had shakes. We thought they were working while he was on it until we wined him over because he was full blown at a 17-month-old baby. Once we took him off we realized nothing was worst then while he was on it
Claire: What has been the hardest part for you?
Emma: I think for me it would be the guilt, the guilt is probably the one thing that’s going to be with me forever. But he gives you hope you know? He my little man he’s so wonderful. And I waited 10 years for him and there’s nothing I wouldn’t do. If I can spare him any pain in this world I will
5 02:36 Claire to camera link. Claire: after trying all the therapies recommended for a child with CP Emma and Nathans parents found ABR, which stands for Advance Biomechanical Rehabilitation. It was discovered by a mechanical engineer from Russia. ABR is available in most parts of the world except for south Africa. Slobodan Vujasic a physical therapist who trains parents on how to use ABR.
6 03:00 Slobodan Vujasic, ABR Specialist Slobodan: ABR is a home based training program, it basically a manual therapy, basically we teach the parents how to apply this therapy to their kids and majority of our patience have cerebral palsy.

Claire: How does the training of the caregivers actually work?

Slobodan: We train the parents, we teach them how to apply on each other. And then after that we teach them how to work on the child to apply the technique on to the child. Then again we asses how they are doing it then we record the whole thing so that they can have it at home =.

Claire: why do you believe ABR is more effective than other treatments?

Slobodan: Since we you have a child with cerebral palsy you immediately go to the neurologist then you go to the therapists that you are specialising in neurology their focus is on the brain, brain, brain and brain.
7 03:42 Erika Erika: ABR is different in the sense that ABR doesn’t focus too much on the brain ABR says lets look at the structure. Instead of looking at this as an electric problem why its not carrying signals lets look at it as a mechanical problem and instead of saying the arm is not moving because a signal not travelling to the arm the arm is not moving because there are mechanical obstructions in the connective tissue actually not allowing the movement to happen. And that there is a fundamental weakness in the core and that’s why she has to use her arms and not stiffen to kind of maintain her position.
8 04:20 Claire Mawisa Claire: ABR is one of the only non invasive therapies for cerebral palsy that can actually change a patients tissue structure on a cellular structure
9 04:31 Slobodan interview with Claire Slobodan: One of the very obvious things for example the child cannot sit independently. Now that child when he sits like this… you move the child the child is falling. If you are sitting and you are falling you are gong to use your spine to fall back and if you don’t have that then you are just a piece of board falling. So the ABR so actually working on the small movements that are happening on the spine that you cannot get anymore

10 04:51 Claire V/O Claire: The gross Moto function classification system measures the severity of patience with cerebral palsy. It starts at one being the least severe and goes down to five being the most severe
11 05:04 Erika speaks to Claire Erika: So basically there are 5 types of CP so Emma is a grade 4, the grade 3-5 are the most severe CP, they are kids who are basically on wheel chairs grade one is almost a typical child. Where ABR is really valuable here is exactly in this more severe category because in these kids you actually have foundational structure
12 05:27 Slobodan interview with Claire Slobodan: we also call this scale doom, the scale of doom basically. The reason why we call it the scale of doom you can see the curve and you can see the desist at the level of 5, six and 7 years old they are stopping with their progress Level one two and three are just staying there at that level but level four and level five are actually regressing.

Claire: What studies have been done with regards to the effectiveness of ABR?

Slobodan: the study has been done in Canada and it lasted for three years with 150 subjects the parents were encouraged for half an hour 5 times a per week and the level of the child’s severity was from level 4 or 5 gross motto function system the reason why they picked these subjects because if we can help them then they are the worst cases obviously se are going to be much more sufficient with the kids that are from the beginning much better. So we manage the level 5 push so far away that they become level 4 and the level 4 improve significantly 8% more than average.
13 06:34 Claire link to camera Claire: With normal therapies used to treat CP normal scale shows that from the age of 8-12 CP children will stop all progress and eventually their condition will get worse whereas with ABR not only are patients improving to the point were they are moving up the scale their progress continues there is no ceiling for ABR therapy as long as the patient is doing the therapy their condition will improve
14 07:02 V/O V/O: the Dewes were living in Europe when they discovered ABR which meant they can access the ABR therapy in Denmark
15 07:09 Erika interview Erika: the first goals were to fix her metabolism to get her repertory system to work, to get her immune function to work her digestive system to work and that was what we saw in the first 6 months to a year she stopped getting sick and started gaining weight the muscle that was completely just a thin strip on the bone started to build out she got nice; little fat arms and fat hands, the shape of her chest started changing, her clothes started fitting her and she started smiling it was alike a light went on. The Emma that had seemed only glimpses of was starting to shine through this very sick body.
16 07:52 Slobodan examining a child as Claire and Carer watch. V/O Claire V/O: After Nathans parents discovered ABR online they made a request to ABR Denmark to send through one of their physical therapist. But without a big enough group of patients they request was denied until Nathan became very ill and the ABR team saw the necessity to send out a trainer to work with Nathan.
17 08:14 Claire interview with the parents Claire: what were the initial benefits you saw using ABR?
James: His body is fuller, his skin looked like paper it feels like you can see right through him you can see his rib bones

Slobodan: Nathan was in pair all the time, Nathan couldn’t communicate. Nathan didn’t react, Nathan didn’t sleep, and whatever position you put him he would be very uncomfortable for a shot period of time. Now Nathan is more relax he’s starting to communicate more easily involved in the whole social environment.
18 08:46 The conclusion of the story by all the guests James: My own opinion is he wouldn’t have survived 2-3 months if we didn’t start that’s how bad he was
Slobodan: It was very stressful for me because I didn’t expect he would be in such a bad condition and the changes are amazing of what happened in the last 6 month with him

Erika: in the beginning when I was doing these other therapies at home, you require the child to perform there was always a sense of failure like she knew she was failing and I know she wasn’t making any progress and there was a disappointment between us and everything is therapy, easting is therapy and sitting on the floor is therapy, building a block is therapy its never just me time like you would have with a typical child. Because with ABR we actually can be a family

The transformation was amazing. You can see his full physical change of the video’s the family have filmed. Nathan can hold himself up for periods of time, he is eating and laughing. Nathan was on various other treatments at the same time though, so medically his improvement can not solely be placed on ABR, but it is his parents’ belief that ABR saved their son.
